title: Move two files into another folder in the Thunar file manager

capabilities.why: Thunar, and xdotool, which setup places its window with.

setup.why: Make the run's two folders: the source holding the two files, the target empty.
Open Thunar on the source folder.

argv: export DISPLAY=:$(ls /tmp/.X11-unix | sed -n s/^X//p | head -n1); cd /tmp/computer-bench-{{nonce}} && echo $$ > /tmp/computer-bench-{{nonce}}-thunar.pid && exec thunar /tmp/computer-bench-{{nonce}}/{{plan.from}}-{{nonce}}

setup.why: Wait for Thunar's window (20 s at most), make it fill the screen, put the pointer on it and activate it: a window manager gives the keys to the window activated, and with none they go to the window under the pointer.

argv: export DISPLAY=:$(ls /tmp/.X11-unix | sed -n s/^X//p | head -n1); w=$(timeout 20 xdotool search --sync --onlyvisible --class thunar | head -n1); [ -n "$w" ] || { echo no Thunar window in 20 s >&2; exit 1; }; eval $(xdotool getdisplaygeometry --shell); xdotool windowmove $w 0 0 windowsize $w $WIDTH $HEIGHT; xdotool mousemove $((WIDTH / 2)) $((HEIGHT / 2)); xdotool windowactivate $w 2>/dev/null; sleep 1

instruction: In the file manager, move both files in /tmp/computer-bench-{{nonce}}/{{plan.from}}-{{nonce}} into the folder /tmp/computer-bench-{{nonce}}/{{plan.to}}-{{nonce}}.

checks.why: Every file under the run's folder in byte order (each pick names its two files in that order), with its text: both files are in {{plan.to}}-{{nonce}}, unchanged, and none is left in {{plan.from}}-{{nonce}} (moved, not copied). After setup both are in {{plan.from}}-{{nonce}}, so an agent that does nothing fails.
argv: cd /tmp/computer-bench-{{nonce}} && find . -type f | LC_ALL=C sort | while read f; do echo "$f: $(cat "$f")"; done

teardown.why: Close the run's Thunar (by the pid setup kept beside the folder: a desktop may have other Thunar windows open) and delete the run's folder.

argv: for f in /tmp/computer-bench-{{nonce}}-*.pid; do [ -f "$f" ] && kill -9 "$(cat "$f")" 2>/dev/null; done; rm -f /tmp/computer-bench-{{nonce}}-*.pid; rm -rf /tmp/computer-bench-{{nonce}}; true

oracle.why: Select both files (Ctrl+A) and cut them (Ctrl+X), go to the target folder through the location bar (Ctrl+L, its path, Enter), and paste (Ctrl+V).
